points.description: States that electron-electron repulsion decreases as each successive electron is removed (repulsion explicitly described as decreasing, not just 'changing').
States explicitly that the decrease in electron-electron repulsion leads to a decrease in potential energy of the remaining electrons.
States that the 3rd and 4th electrons removed both come from the n = 3 shell and feel the same core charge, so they have the same radius.
States that the 5th electron removed comes from the n = 2 shell, feels a higher core charge than the 3rd and 4th electrons, and therefore has a smaller radius.
Explains the relationship between potential energy and ionization energy: lower potential energy of the electron means more energy is needed to remove it, so the ionization energy is higher.

rubric.notes: Full marks need every element stated explicitly with the correct terms: repulsion decreasing, the link to lower potential energy, the same core charge and n = 3 shell with same radius for the 3rd and 4th electrons, and the higher core charge, n = 2 shell and smaller radius for the 5th electron, plus the explicit link from potential energy to a higher ionization energy. A point is earned only if its full claim is stated; a half-stated point (for example only one of the two facts in P3 or P4) earns nothing, because this is not clearly more than half of the point. A wrong statement within a point, such as saying the 5th electron is in the n = 3 shell or that the core charge is the same for all five electrons, cancels that point. Restating the question or giving a general definition of ionization energy earns nothing.
